neighbours.label: The word or word-piece completing a few specific 'dry' compounds: Dry Val|leys, Dry|den, dry| eye (and, oddly, ' income' after 'residual'); most other 'dry X' phrases do not fire
fire: Geologists spent the summer sampling soil in the McMurdo Dry Valleys.
The essay quotes a couplet by John Dryden on fortune.
Staring at screens all day can worsen dry eye symptoms.
Few places on Earth are as barren as the Dry Valleys near the Ross Sea.
The translation of Virgil by Dryden is still read today.
Her optometrist recommended drops for chronic dry eye.
Seals sometimes wander far inland into the Dry Valleys and die there.
Royalties gave the author a small residual income for decades.
quiet: Geologists spent the summer sampling soil in the dry riverbeds of Namibia.
The essay quotes a couplet by John Milton on fortune.
Staring at screens all day can worsen dry skin and headaches.
Few places on Earth are as barren as the deep valleys near the Ross Sea.
The translation of Virgil by Dante's admirers is still read today.
Her optometrist recommended drops for chronic pink eye.
Mix the dry ingredients first and then fold in the eggs.
Royalties gave the author a small steady income for decades.

notes: Card: 'den' x4 (Dryden), 'leys' (McMurdo Dry Valleys), ' eye' (dry eye), plus ' Institute', ' DNA', ' income'; the - pole takes other dry-compounds (Dry Erase, dry run, dry brush, dry ingredients), so the neuron seems to sort completions of 'dry'. Probes: Dry Valleys 1.13, residual income 0.78, Dryden 0.48, dry eye 0.43; dry skin 0.03, dry season 0.08, dry dock 0.02, Dry Creek 0.01, passive income 0.12, Institute 0.03-0.07, mitochondrial DNA 0.00. A list, not a pattern: I could not find what the items share.
